title: Texas's 38th Congressional District election, 2026
description: An open-seat race in Texas's 38th Congressional District, which covers western and northwestern Harris County including the Houston suburbs of Cypress, Tomball, Jersey Village, and parts of the city's wealthier neighborhoods such as River Oaks. The seat became open after incumbent Republican Wesley Hunt ran unsuccessfully for U.S. Senate. The district was redrawn in a controversial mid-decade redistricting process that was briefly blocked by a federal court before the U.S. Supreme Court allowed it. Rated 'Solid R' by the Cook Political Report, the district was designed as a Republican stronghold when created after the 2020 Census, but Democrat Melissa McDonough is appealing to moderate voters with a 'purple' message emphasizing checks and balances, while Republican nominee Jon Bonck runs as a Trump-endorsed conservative focused on border security, religious liberty, and fiscal issues.
polling_note: No district-specific general election polls were found for this race as of June 2026. A University of Houston Hobby School poll from February 2026 surveyed the Republican primary field but not the general election matchup.

candidates.name: Jon Bonck
candidates.summary: Jon Bonck is a mortgage banker and real estate broker from Houston who won the Republican nomination in a May 2026 runoff after leading a 10-candidate primary field. Endorsed by President Donald Trump and Senator Ted Cruz, Bonck campaigns as a Christian conservative focused on border security, religious liberty, and cutting government spending. He serves as a deacon and Bible study teacher at Second Baptist Church.

candidates.name: Melissa McDonough
candidates.summary: Melissa McDonough is a realtor and small business owner from Tomball who won the Democratic nomination outright with 51.6% of the vote in the March 2026 primary. She has nearly 30 years of experience as a REALTOR and 20 years as a real estate brokerage owner/manager, and has lobbied Congress for consumer protection and healthcare on behalf of the National Association of Realtors. Her campaign focuses on restoring congressional checks and balances, affordable healthcare, and effective border management.

candidates.name: William Taggart
candidates.summary: William Taggart (also known as Butch) is an Independent candidate running for U.S. House in Texas' 38th Congressional District. He is an engineer and author of 'Fixing America – An Engineer's Solution to our Social, Cultural, and Political Problems,' and campaigns as a moderate independent focused on healthcare, housing, energy costs, and tax reform.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific general election polling exists as of June 2026 (the only available survey was a University of Houston Hobby School poll focused on the Republican primary). Without polling, the forecast relies on structural and contextual factors. TX-38 was designed as a Republican stronghold after the 2020 Census, is rated 'Solid R' by Cook Political Report, and covers affluent and suburban areas of western/northwestern Harris County that lean Republican. The seat became open after Wesley Hunt (R) vacated it for an unsuccessful Senate run, but the district's partisan baseline remains strongly Republican. Jon Bonck secured the Republican nomination in a competitive 10-candidate primary and runoff with endorsements from Trump and Cruz, while Democratic nominee Melissa McDonough is running a moderate 'purple' message. However, in a district drawn to elect Republicans and with no polling evidence of a competitive shift, the Republican candidate holds an overwhelming structural advantage. Third-party candidates (Green, Independent) are on the ballot but not competitive. Confidence is medium due to the absence of any general election polling data.
